claim: The EndpointPickerConfig supports 'Auto-Wiring': if a plugin declared in the top-level plugins list implements a specific Go interface -- Admitter, DataProducer, or hooks like PreRequest, ResponseHeaderProcessor, ResponseBodyProcessor -- the system automatically discovers and binds it to its lifecycle role without an explicit wiring edge elsewhere in the config.
stance_target: how plugins are registered/bound -- confirming an interface-reflection auto-binding layer sits on top of compile-time Go registration
scope_conditions: llm-d dev docs, EPP Configuration reference
quoted_support: If a plugin is declared in the top-level plugins list and implements a specific Go interface (like Admitter, DataProducer, or advanced hooks like PreRequest, ResponseHeaderProcessor, and ResponseBodyProcessor), the system will automatically discover and bind it to its role without requiring an explicit edge in the structural configuration.

claim: The config graph is validated for internal consistency: all pluginRef fields must resolve to a name defined in the top-level plugins section, names in lists like schedulingProfiles must be unique and non-empty, and metrics extractors must form a Directed Acyclic Graph with no circular data dependencies.
stance_target: the validation contract a custom plugin/config must satisfy to load successfully
scope_conditions: llm-d dev docs, EPP Configuration reference
quoted_support: The system validates that metrics extractors form a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) without circular dependencies, ensuring correct execution order.

claim: Scheduling profile execution order is fixed and enforced by the framework regardless of YAML plugin list order: Filters run first, then Scorers, then exactly one Picker; referencing more than one Picker in a profile causes a runtime initialization error.
stance_target: exact execution-order contract for the Filter/Scorer/Picker plugin taxonomy
scope_conditions: llm-d dev docs, EPP Configuration reference, Profile Execution Rules
quoted_support: Execution Order: Plugins are executed in this order: Filters first, then Scorers, and finally the Picker. Multiple Pickers: A scheduling profile cannot have more than one picker.

claim: A Profile Handler plugin is only required when multiple SchedulingProfiles are defined (e.g. disaggregated prefill needing separate prefill/decode profiles); with a single profile, SingleProfileHandler is implicitly used and requires no explicit configuration.
stance_target: when the ProfileHandler plugin type must be explicitly configured versus defaulted
scope_conditions: llm-d dev docs, EPP Configuration reference
quoted_support: Profile Handler: When multiple profiles are defined, you must instantiate and configure a Profile Handler plugin in the top-level plugins section. ... Single Profile Default: If only one profile is defined, the system implicitly uses a SingleProfileHandler

claim: The default metrics-data-source and core-metrics-extractor injection into dataLayer is additive, not exclusive: even when a user supplies their own dataLayer.sources, the default metrics source is appended unless injectDefaults is set false or the user's config already contains a metrics-data-source entry -- meaning a custom non-k8s DataSource added by a user will run ALONGSIDE the default pod-metrics scraper unless explicitly suppressed.
stance_target: a concrete operational gotcha for anyone adding a custom DataSource: the default pod-based one keeps running unless explicitly disabled
scope_conditions: llm-d dev docs, EPP Configuration reference, dataLayer section
quoted_support: Injection is additive — even when you supply your own dataLayer, the default metrics source is appended with your sources. Unless you set injectDefaults: false or dataLayer.sources already contains a metrics-data-source source

stance_target: documentation currency/consistency across llm-d.ai vs llm-d-router repo docs, relevant given the run's 12-18 month recency directive
quoted_support: For full details and a list of available data sources and extractors, see the Data Layer reference (TODO: add link to datalayer.md once written).

claim: EPP high availability is active-passive: setting replicas>1 elects a single leader via leader election, and only that leader replica processes traffic at any given time (not active-active load sharing across replicas).
stance_target: HA model constraint relevant to scaling a customized EPP deployment
scope_conditions: llm-d dev docs, EPP Configuration reference, High Availability section
quoted_support: To deploy the EndpointPicker in a high-availability (HA) active-passive configuration, set replicas to be greater than one. In such a setup, only one "leader" replica will be active and ready to process traffic at any given time.
